content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss threats across identities, data, availability, and permissions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through structured STRIDE analysis and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Defines when to use STRIDE for threat modeling, design review, training, and audit preparation.
Explains spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and elevation categories.
Provides a threat model document template with assets, trust boundaries, STRIDE tables, risk scoring, and recommendations.
Includes Python examples for representing threats, assets, trust boundaries, and report summaries.
Offers data flow and interaction analysis templates for mapping threats to system elements.
limitations: Does not perform automated scanning or validate live system controls.
Requires accurate architecture, asset, data flow, and trust boundary inputs.
Examples are templates and must be adapted before production security decisions.
Does not replace specialist review for regulated or high-risk systems.

use_cases.title: Model threats for a new service
use_cases.description: Create a STRIDE threat model for a new API, including assets, trust boundaries, risks, and mitigations.

use_cases.title: Review architecture before build
use_cases.description: Check data flows and trust boundaries before implementation to find missing authentication, logging, and encryption controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare security documentation
use_cases.description: Produce structured threat documentation that supports audit preparation, control discussions, and engineering follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic STRIDE Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a known system
prompt_templates.prompt: Use STRIDE to review this system. Ask for missing architecture details, then list threats by category with practical mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Data Flow Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of components and trust boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this data flow diagram with STRIDE. Identify trust boundaries, sensitive assets, likely threats, and control gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Threats and Mitigations
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this STRIDE threat list into prioritized risks. Include impact, likelihood, mitigation owner, and next review step.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Audit-Ready Threat Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an audit-ready STRIDE threat model for this architecture. Include assumptions, assets, trust boundaries, risks, mitigations, and unresolved questions.

output_examples.input: A web app sends user requests through an API gateway to backend services and a database.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies spoofing risks at login, tampering risks on API requests, disclosure risks in database access, and denial risks at shared services.

output_examples.input: A team needs a threat model before a compliance review.
output: System overview with key assets and trust boundaries.
STRIDE threat tables grouped by category.
Prioritized mitigation plan with short-term and long-term actions.

output_examples.input: An architect wants to check whether a new payment flow has missing controls.
output_examples.output: The skill maps interactions to STRIDE categories, flags sensitive trust boundary crossings, and proposes authentication, logging, encryption, and rate-limit controls.

best_practices: Provide system purpose, assets, users, data flows, and trust boundaries before starting analysis.
Review each STRIDE category separately so common threat classes are not skipped.
Turn each threat into a concrete mitigation, owner, and verification step.
anti_patterns: Using STRIDE only as a checklist without documenting assumptions and evidence.
Skipping low-likelihood threats before impact and compensating controls are understood.
Treating template output as final approval without engineering and security review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me produce?
faq.answer: It helps produce STRIDE threat models, threat tables, risk priorities, mitigation plans, and security review notes.

faq.question: Does it scan source code or infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It is a guidance and documentation skill, not an automated scanner.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the system purpose, users, assets, data flows, trust boundaries, authentication model, and existing controls.

faq.question: Can it support compliance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize threat evidence and mitigation plans for audit preparation, but it does not replace formal compliance review.

faq.question: Is this useful for early design reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It is strongest when used before implementation, when architecture and control decisions can still change.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
